small_guidance:
- The fused gemm_logsumexp_kernel uses BLOCK_N = next_pow2(1024) = 1024 with BLOCK_M up to 128 and BLOCK_K up to 64, producing a (128,1024) acc tile plus large A/B staging — that blows past 100KB shared mem. Cap BLOCK_M at 32 (or 16) and BLOCK_K at 32 with num_stages=2 in the autotune configs for this kernel, so the (BLOCK_M, 1024) accumulator and pipelined K-loads fit in 101KB shared memory.
- Drop the largest configs entirely (BLOCK_M=128, BLOCK_K=64, num_stages=4) for gemm_logsumexp_kernel — keep only e.g. {BLOCK_M:16/32, BLOCK_K:32, num_warps:4/8, num_stages:2}.
- Optionally reduce BLOCK_N to 512 and do the LSE reduction in 2 chunks (track running max/sumexp across two N-tiles) to free shared memory and allow bigger BLOCK_M for better M-side parallelism.
large_guidance:
- Split the second linear+logsumexp into two kernels: a tiled GEMM (M,N)=(16384,1024), K=4096 writing the full activation tile, then a separate row-wise logsumexp kernel. The GEMM gets standard tile shapes (128×128×32) and the LSE kernel is a cheap 1024-wide reduction. Keeps shared-memory pressure decoupled from the N=1024 reduction width.
- Alternatively, do an online (streaming) logsumexp fused into the GEMM: tile over N as well as M, maintain per-row running (max, sum_exp) in registers, update with the standard log-sum-exp merge each N-tile. This keeps the accumulator small (BLOCK_M × BLOCK_N with BLOCK_N=128 or 256) and avoids the (BLOCK_M, 1024) tile that is overflowing shared memory.
- Consider a persistent-row strategy for the second stage since M=16384 is large and N=1024 is modest: one program per row group reads its hidden slice once, accumulates the matmul into a (BLOCK_M, BLOCK_N) tile, and folds into the LSE state — eliminating the activation materialization.
